The Great Wall of China has two ends. On the eastern end, the wall terminates at Shanhaiguan (also called Shanhai Pass), located outside Qinhuangdao City on Bohai Bay [d4][d6]. More specifically, the easternmost point where the wall meets the sea is called Laolongtou (Old Dragon's Head), which is part of the Shanhai Pass complex and was built in 1381 under Ming-dynasty general Qi Jiguang [d2]. On the western end, the wall terminates at Jiayuguan (Jiayu Pass) in modern Gansu province, described as the first frontier fortress at the western end of the Great Wall in the Ming Dynasty [d4][d6][d8]. However, d7 adds an important nuance: while Shanhaiguan is commonly cited as the eastern end, the Ming Great Wall actually extended further to Hushan in Liaoning province on the Manchu/Korean border [d7].
